title: trek.py: what the trek does when a chain ends (usage limits first)
about: Task W132 (stop at a usage limit) on top of the trek. A trek starts work chains, one task each, on a session budget. Each tick it judges the chains that ended: trek_decide turns a chain's stop cause into run, hold, stop, raise or pend. A usage limit is the one cause the trek waits out and retries; stop_on_limit ends the trek there instead.

trek_spent += the sessions the ended chain ran
removes the judged chain's record
adds a record for each chain it starts
on hold: the later of the old hold and the reset time, or now + 3600 s when the text cannot be read
before this time, return without starting anything
adds the item, remembering whether the author pinned it; trek_lead keeps a carried draft only if it was pinned
removes a task as its next chain starts
clears the pin just before start_chain is called, so a start that fails still loses it
remembers tasks a stop break held, unless keep is False
trek_spent plus the current run number of each of this trek's chains that dfs_runs can see, ended but not yet judged ones included
trek_pending = True when nothing is picked and no chain of the trek or of another is running, back to False when a chain is about to start
each new chain's cap is what is left after live chains' caps, divided by the slots still to fill (rounded down, at least 1): 20 left and 3 free gives 6, 7, 7
charges the sessions actually run; the unused part of the cap is free again
one slot per chain; hand-started chains count against them

writes the cap file of each live chain trek_off just dropped, lowered to the run it is on, so it ends after that run; nothing judges it, so it is outside this trek's budget and slots, and a later trek counts it as a chain it did not start (trek_foreign) until it ends
a daemon thread every 300 s; skipped while the last is still running
stop action (a limit with stop_on_limit, or a cause only a person can judge) → the whole trek ends
idle, or a blocked or capped chain that moved nothing (not done) → a raise on that item; the other tasks go on if the raise succeeds
the raise cannot be written, or next_item still names the item → the trek ends
the trek ending drops every chain from trek_chains, then each live one is told to end after the run it is on
a chain still not on the box after 15 s → the trek ends, with console.log's cause
start_chain returns None → the trek ends; chains already started are told to end, except one started in this same tick that dfs_runs cannot see yet

a chain whose cap file cannot be written is returned in a list; only stopping by hand (trek_end_chain) reads it and names the first; every automatic trek_off drops the list, so that chain keeps running to its old cap and nobody is told
a pull request that cannot be read is an event line; the trek goes on
console.log unreadable (OSError) → chain_cause returns '', so trek_off's reason carries no cause and nobody is told
a task that ended on its cap, or was held by a limit, goes to the front next time
in order: the pin, each carried task still workable, then the roadmap's next item
as many as there are free slots; a task that would share the one checkout with a running chain is passed over
nothing workable → the trek stays on and asks again each tick; nothing is spent
during a hold nothing new starts, but chains that ended are still judged
